newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strike won't affect soy loading at Paranagua - port.
newsitem.headline: Strike won't affect soy loading at Paranagua - port.

text.p: Shipments of Brazilian soybeans, soymeal and corn will be unaffected even if workers at the key port of Paranagua decide to go on strike March 5, the port authority said.
"The loading of grains is made by conveyor belts, it is all automated," a spokeswoman said. "With five people you can operate the export terminal (which handles grains)."

The port authority was confident the export terminal would continue to operate because even if port workers strike, their section chiefs will provide the necessary manpower to keep the terminal running, the spokeswoman said.
Dock workers at the port were due to meet port operators on Tuesday to try to avert a threatened strike.
The workers are demanding a 21 percent wage increase which they say they are owed since last year.
The spokeswoman also confirmed that dock workers had scaled down their operations and this was affecting general cargo which relies on manual labor including wood, orange juice and cotton.
"They are operating on a work to rule basis since 0700 local time (1000 GMT) on Monday," she said.
Other workers have also had to scale down their operations as a result, she said but she could not say to what extent port operations had been affected.
